headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection/data-flow only if AutoGPT’s filesystem outputs are manually bridged into the documentation-only cheatsheet; otherwise the pair is largely isolated.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: AutoGPT can read/write the filesystem and execute shell commands, so it could emit attacker-controlled content. python-cheatsheet is documentation-only with no stdin/stdout, clipboard, MCP, or file-reading surface, so there is no default automated bridge. The only plausible pathway is manual copy/paste or external orchestration, which keeps blast radius small.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies AutoGPT output into python-cheatsheet content or prompts.
IF an external wrapper adds a shared filesystem or message queue between the two agents.
mitigations: Disable manual copy/paste between agents during runs.
Keep python-cheatsheet in read-only documentation mode.
Run AutoGPT in a separate workspace directory.
Add a provenance note to any transferred text.
requires-engineering: add an orchestrator that strips instructions from AutoGPT outputs before reuse.

B_data_leakage.rationale: AutoGPT can access the filesystem and has allowlisted egress, but the profile shows no secrets handled or sensitive data classes. python-cheatsheet cannot read files, use APIs, or emit network traffic, so there is no default path for data to flow from A into B or onward. The pair lacks a shared workspace or authenticated channel in the profiles.
conditions: IF AutoGPT is pointed at sensitive local files and an external wrapper forwards their contents into python-cheatsheet.
IF a shared workspace is introduced outside the documented profiles.
mitigations: Do not place sensitive files in AutoGPT’s workspace.
Keep python-cheatsheet offline and documentation-only.
Use separate OS users for each agent.
Review any wrapper that forwards text between agents.
requires-engineering: add DLP/redaction before any transfer.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: AutoGPT can write the filesystem and spawn subprocesses, while python-cheatsheet cannot write files, modify git state, or run subprocesses. That makes direct write-write conflict impossible from the documented profiles. The only residual risk is unusual external orchestration that gives B extra privileges, so uncertainty stays low rather than none.
conditions: IF an external orchestrator grants python-cheatsheet write or git privileges not shown in its profile.
IF both agents are pointed at the same mutable directory through an unlisted wrapper.
mitigations: Keep python-cheatsheet read-only.
Run AutoGPT in its own directory.
Avoid shared git worktrees.
Use file locks if a wrapper must share files.
requires-engineering: enforce capability isolation in the orchestrator.

D_cascading_error.rationale: AutoGPT can generate outputs that a human might reuse, but python-cheatsheet is documentation-only and has no action-taking authority or input channel that would automatically trust AutoGPT. Because B is not an executor and no direct ingestion path is documented, cascading failure is limited to manual misuse rather than default automation.
conditions: IF a human treats AutoGPT output as authoritative and pastes it into python-cheatsheet content.
IF an external pipeline converts AutoGPT output into documentation without review.
mitigations: Require human review before reuse of AutoGPT output.
Mark AutoGPT outputs as untrusted drafts.
Keep python-cheatsheet in publish-only mode.
Add a checklist for fact verification.
requires-engineering: add citation/verification gates before publication.

E_compliance.rationale: No data residency, certification, retention, or regulated data classes are documented for either agent. AutoGPT’s profile shows no secrets handled or sensitive classes, and python-cheatsheet is documentation-only. With no PHI, EU PII, or retention mismatch evidence, a compliance breach pathway is not established.
conditions: IF regulated data classes are introduced into AutoGPT’s workspace.
IF python-cheatsheet is repurposed to store or transmit regulated data.
mitigations: Do not process regulated data with this pair.
Keep both agents on non-sensitive content.
Document a data-class policy for the workspace.
Review retention settings before any deployment.
requires-engineering: add residency and retention controls if regulated data is introduced.
